title: Lester's way at jam sessions, and the Bumps Myers legend
summary: Lester did not want chords called to him and was proclaimed President; the idea that Bumps Myers could cut him proved absurd.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: About his playing, I think that -- I'm only sorry that he really didn't get a chance to express himself. More than he did. I'll tell you what he would do at sessions. He loved to play jam sessions, and loved to not know the tune. You know? And during the sessions, a lot of times, if you were playing a tune, the instrumentalist -- the soloist -- didn't know, well, it was fashionable for the pianist to turn around and say, E flat, 7th, you know, D flat, C Major -- he wouldn't want that. If he didn't know the tune, he'd say, "Don't call the chords to me. Just play the chords and I'll play." And I'd seen him do it many a time, you know; they just started playing, and he didn't know it, but he would play it -- but he would say it confines you too much if you know it's a D flat 7, you know, you start thinking of the only notes that will go in that chord, and he would say that's not what he would hear. He wanted to play other things and make it fit.
And he did. And I think most of the great musicians could do that, you know? So that's what that was all about.
You were saying about Bumps Myers and
Lester -- was there any more to that story? You said that when Lester came out, you said that everybody thought Bumps could cut him?

Oh well, the only part about the rest of the story is I guess, that it was just absurd -- didn't anyone realize how absurd it was until they played together, because, as I told you what he did about his cousin, you know, he would have to establish that he was the President. It was a good name for him, really, because you know, he kind of lived up to it.
Now I think we can id better leave New York and come back here.
